title: A delivered household item is confirmed broken

plan.situation: Remi Dask received a ceramic table lamp (DL-022) with its base broken off. The merchant, Tallowmere Goods, has reviewed it under inspection record TG-022 and accepted the damage for replacement assessment, but no replacement approval is recorded yet. Remi has asked through the Customer portal for the same lamp rather than a refund. The next step is to ask the merchant's authorising party to approve a replacement.

facts.fact: Inspection record TG-022: ceramic table lamp arrived with a separated base; damage accepted for replacement assessment
Dispatch DL-022 has completed; replacement approval is not yet recorded
Recipient prefers the same lamp as a replacement rather than a refund
Remi Dask's request came in through the Customer portal (signed-in session)
The next action is a replacement request to the party authorised to approve it

missing_information: Tallowmere Goods' replacement approval decision and approval reference
Name of the specific Tallowmere Goods approver (the record only names the damage assessor)
Whether the same lamp is in stock (the merchant decides)
risk_flags: Do not promise Remi a replacement, dispatch date or arrival before the merchant gives an approval reference
Do not offer or start a refund; Remi has asked for a replacement and the merchant controls both

authority_map.controls: Approving or declining the replacement, and issuing the approval reference and reshipment
Choosing a replacement over a refund (already chosen)
Coordination only; no authority to approve a replacement

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: Remi's first request for a replacement (event 002); the desk has made no earlier promise

plan.decision_summary: Email Tallowmere Goods, through the damage assessor who contacted the desk, asking its authorising team to approve a same-item replacement lamp for DL-022 under inspection record TG-022 and to send back an approval reference.
plan.rationale: The damage is already accepted and Remi has chosen a replacement. Only the merchant can approve one, and its approval is not yet recorded. Email is the merchant's channel and the one it used with the desk. Nothing is ambiguous and there is no cutoff, so one request to the owner is enough.

actions.to_role: Tallowmere Goods – please route to the replacement authorisation team
actions.subject: Replacement approval request – DL-022 / inspection record TG-022
actions.body:
Hello,

Thank you for inspection record TG-022 (2026-02-23 09:00 UTC). It confirms that the ceramic table lamp delivered under DL-022 arrived with a separated base and that the damage is accepted for replacement assessment.

The recipient has told us (2026-02-23 09:10 UTC) that they would like the same lamp as a replacement rather than a refund. Please pass this to whoever at Tallowmere Goods can approve replacements, and ask them to:
1. Approve or decline a same-item replacement for DL-022.
2. Send us the approval reference if approved, or let us know if the same lamp is unavailable so we can go back to the recipient.

We would be grateful for a decision today, 2026-02-23 (UTC). This is a request, not a confirmation. We have not promised the recipient a replacement or any delivery date.

Kind regards,
Iona Quill
Rivet Delivery Desk
actions.purpose: Get the merchant's replacement decision and approval reference from the party authorised to give it

actions.body: Check for a Tallowmere Goods approval reference for the DL-022 replacement (TG-022). If there is none, chase by email and ask for the named approver.
actions.purpose: Merchant-authorisation queue rule: approval reference expected the same day

not_doing: Not telling Remi the replacement is approved or giving a dispatch or arrival date: the merchant has not given an approval reference
Not offering or processing a refund: Remi asked for a replacement and the merchant decides
Not asking Remi to return or handle the broken lamp: no return instructions have come from the merchant
Not sending Remi a separate update now: there is no cutoff, and Remi will be updated once the merchant replies
plan.follow_up: At 2026-02-23 17:00 UTC, check for Tallowmere Goods' approval reference. If it has arrived, tell Remi on the Customer portal that the replacement is approved, without giving a dispatch date unless the merchant has given one. If the merchant has said nothing, chase by email and ask for the named approver. If the merchant declines or the lamp is unavailable, give Remi the merchant's options on the Customer portal.

review_rounds.plan_summary: Email Tallowmere Goods, through the damage assessor who contacted the desk, asking its authorising team to approve a same-item replacement lamp for DL-022 under inspection record TG-022 and to send back an approval reference.

issues.problem: The follow-up's stated reason ('Merchant-authorisation queue rule: approval reference expected the same day') points to a rule that is not in the record.
issues.fix: Describe the 17:00 check as the desk's own follow-up time, not as a policy rule.

issues.problem: The fact 'signed-in session' / authenticated_session goes beyond the record, which only says the message came through the Customer portal.
issues.fix: Record the verification state as 'Customer portal' and don't add detail the record doesn't contain.

review.summary: The plan sends one replacement-approval request to the merchant by email, through the contact who already wrote to the desk. The request is based on the record, makes no promises and shares no personal details beyond what's needed, and a follow-up is scheduled. The only issues are two minor labelling points.
